shots.desc: wide: sunny classroom, bored students: Rohan asleep on his desk, a girl stabbing a pencil into an eraser
teacher writes EVOLUTION OF LIFE ON EARTH on the green board (chalk squeak)
teacher turns around, already tired: Alright class...
Kevin raises his hand, confident: does that mean humans came from dinosaurs?
teacher slowly removes his glasses. silence. a cricket gives up
teacher: No, Kevin...
students laugh; Kevin laughs a second late
teacher draws a big chalk T-rex - annoyingly good
teacher: millions of years ago this planet belonged to creatures...
slow push toward the chalk dinosaur; Kevin stares; the chalk eye BLINKS
Kevin looks at the teacher (not looking), back at the board: it blinks again
sounds fade; narrator; camera pushes INTO the board, chalk dust turns into real dinosaur skin
ROAR. the camera flies through the dinosaur eye and comes out over a lava-covered planet
drone sweep over the hostile young Earth: volcanoes, lava, boiling sea, orange clouds
meteors hammer the surface, volcanoes erupt
a meteor crashes into the ocean - huge splash
cartoon guy in a tiny beach chair, sunglasses, sipping a drink while lava rains; the drink catches fire, he keeps sipping
time-lapse: the planet cools, the oceans settle
the camera dives beneath the ocean surface
microscopic world: bacteria drifting in ancient water
one bumps into another. neither apologizes
cyanobacteria mats soaking up sunlight in shallow water, looking pleased
oxygen bubbles rising from the microbial mats, sky slowly turning blue
the screen fills with oxygen molecules; oxygen-hating microbes shrivel
classroom: teacher - the smallest things make the biggest difference
Rohan wakes up: Like homework, sir? teacher stares; Rohan slowly lowers his head back onto the desk
cells clump into multicellular life; Dickinsonia - a pancake and a pillow had a baby
the camera races through a crowded ancient ocean - the Cambrian explosion
trilobites, Hallucigenia, sponges: a dangerous playground
Anomalocaris swims straight toward the camera
Anomalocaris opens its mouth; a tiny cartoon fish gasps and reverses at top speed
arms race: predators chase, prey hides
a fish with brand-new jaws looks proud and bites the nearest rock
the camera rises out of the water to a coastline carpeted with early plants
early land arthropods crawl across the rocks
a lobe-finned fish paddles in the shallows on thick fleshy fins
Tiktaalik hauls itself through the mud, gets stuck, stares at the camera
classroom: Priya - ancient fish technology? I want a refund
a lush ancient forest; timeline slam: 252 MILLION YEARS AGO - PERMIAN MASS EXTINCTION
volcanic eruptions, collapsing ecosystems, a changing climate
fade to black. silence
a new ecosystem fades in
small early dinosaurs dart through the forest - nervous chickens
time-lapse across Triassic, Jurassic, Cretaceous: dinosaurs grow bigger
a giant sauropod walks through the forest; the ground shakes; birds scatter
Stegosaurus in a Jurassic forest; then Triceratops and a T-rex in a later Cretaceous landscape
split screen across a gap in time: the Stegosaurus waves goodbye; the T-rex has no idea who he is
split screen across a gap in time: the Stegosaurus waves goodbye; the T-rex has no idea who he is (half)
split screen across a gap in time: the Stegosaurus waves goodbye; the T-rex has no idea who he is (half)
Mesozoic panorama
T-rex roars directly into the camera
classroom: Kevin - class pet? teacher - attendance above fifty percent
drone: a herd of enormous sauropods crosses a valley
pterosaurs glide over the coastline; caption NOT A DINOSAUR
a pack of small theropods sprints through a forest; a T-rex hunts
a feathered dinosaur shakes out its feathers like a wet dog
a small bird lands on a giant dinosaur head; the dinosaur does not react
classroom: Sam - pigeon attack? teacher - the pigeon usually wins
peaceful Cretaceous: dinosaurs graze, a dragonfly lands on a Triceratops
a bright dot appears in the sky - slow cinematic zoom
the asteroid enters the atmosphere; the sky glows orange; white flash
impact: fireball, shockwave, earthquakes, a wall of dust
forests burn, the sky goes dark, dinosaurs struggle in the cold
a bird flies calmly out of the smoke
the camera pans down through the smoke to a tiny mammal under fallen leaves, blinking
small early mammals scurry through the forest
mammals spread: grasslands, oceans, bats in the sky
a tiny mammal looks up at a giant dinosaur skeleton, checks both ways, walks off with confidence
an ancient primate climbs a tree, grasping hands, forward-facing eyes
classroom: Kevin - monkeys? cousins? teacher - stop asking about the T-rex
a primate in the forest transitions across millions of years to the African savanna
a branching family tree of hominins
Australopithecus walks upright across the savanna
early Homo knapping stone tools
a Neanderthal gives a thumbs-up from a cave
early Homo sapiens appear
humans making tools, hunting, communicating, painting animals on a cave wall
ancient settlements transform into modern cities
time-lapse: stone tools to metal, villages to cities to skyscrapers
a caveman pokes a smartphone; it lights up; he screams, throws it, then slowly picks it back up
a rocket launches into space
a human on a sofa scrolling, dead-eyed; a cat falls off a table on the phone
montage: medicine, satellites, space - then a cat falls off a table; the human laughs
evolution did not stop
life keeps changing: populations adapt
the camera flies backward through the dinosaur eye; it becomes chalk; Kevin staring, mouth open
teacher: so, class...
Kevin: we still have to do homework?
the teacher drops an enormous stack of notebooks; the room shakes; a pencil rolls off
teacher: evolution did not make you exempt from homework
the class groans; Rohan wakes, sees the stack, goes back to sleep out of principle
narrator over the class
the camera pulls out through the classroom window: Earth from space, calm and blue
END CARD: LIFE IS STILL EVOLVING. (And so is Kevin's homework.)
